lines: Uncle. Is it true a thornback can knock down an oak?
A young one, maybe. An old one knocks down the man behind it.
I'd step aside. Like the Guild folk do.
You'd trip over your own axe. Eat your bread.
Forty cords by the frost. We're at twenty-two.
Twenty-three. I split one more while you were snoring at noon.
Corwin wants twelve more blocks for the Guild wall by the new moon.
Corwin can come up here and cut them himself.
They are square. It's the wall that's crooked.
Heard the crane creak today. Grease it tomorrow.
That wasn't the crane. That was your knees.
Forty years walking to shrines, old man. What do you pray for?
Good roads. And for peddlers to sell something useful.
And has one ever been lucky?
Off to the shrine again? Take some bread, you'll fall over on the road.
The shrine has never once made you breakfast.
I'm the adventurer, you be the goblin.
I was the goblin yesterday! You be the goblin.
Goblins don't say rrrargh. They go hee-hee-hee.
The cows don't care about the fence, uncle.
That's what the fence is for.
